newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec City funicular crash injures 16 tourists.
newsitem.headline: Quebec City funicular crash injures 16 tourists.

text.p: Police said Saturday that 16 tourists were injured when a funicular railway passenger car fell 20 feet (six metres) in the historic old section of Quebec City.

Darie Bertrand, spokeswoman for the Quebec City Police, told Reuters that the accident happened at 3:50 p.m. (1950 GMT) when the railcar's cable released. The funicular railway descends 200 feet (61 metres) from the Chateau Frontenac hotel overlooking the St. Lawrence River to the lower part of the former garrison city.
"There were 16 people in the funicular, all were injured and taken to hospital," Bertrand said.

Eight of the passengers were seriously injured, but the injuries did not appear life-threatening, she said. "Several of them have serious injuries to the legs, arms hips and ankles because the funicular's windows shattered," she said.
The injured, all of whom were foreign tourists, were taken to local hospitals.
The funicular railway uses a system of rails and cables to raise and lower the passenger cabin from the promenade in front of the Chateau Frontenac.
